original_question: Fix a finite set S of places of Q, and let Qtot,S be the maximal extension of Q in which every place in S is totally split. Is the field Qtot,S intersected with Qsolv pseudo S-closed (PSC), where a subfield K of Qtot,S is PSC if every smooth Q-variety that has a point over Qp for each p in S (with Q_infinity = R) has a K-rational point?
target_in_paper: The solvable-case half of Conjecture 1.1, read together with the introductory reformulation/context in Proposition 1.2 and the partial evidence in Theorem 1.3, and revisited in §3 ("Algebraic fields").
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient arithmetic setting (a finite set S of places of Q, the totally S-split field Q_{tot,S}, and the maximal solvable extension Q_{solv}), and it correctly recognizes that the paper’s question is not merely about ampleness but about the stronger local-global/PSC property for the intersection field. It also correctly notes the role of the places in S and the convention Q_\infty=R.
missing_details: The paper’s target is the solvable part of a named introductory conjecture (Conjecture 1.1), not an isolated ad hoc question.
The relevant field should be named explicitly as K:=Q_{tot,S} \cap Q_{solv}.
Q_{solv} should be defined paper-faithfully as the compositum of all finite solvable extensions of Q (equivalently, the maximal prosolvable extension of Q).
Q_{tot,S} should be defined as the maximal algebraic extension of Q in which every place in S is totally split.

The PSC condition should be stated in the paper’s own local-global form, namely with respect to the classical closures/local factors above the places in S, rather than only informally as having Q_p-points.
Your draft formulates PSC using arbitrary smooth Q-varieties; the paper’s nearby introductory formulation is sharper and should be stated in the paper’s exact scope rather than broadened.
The official formulation is the solvable variant of a parallel abelian/solvable pair of questions; that context is implicit in your draft but should be made explicit.
The quantifiers should be stated cleanly: for every finite set S of places of Q, does the corresponding intersection field satisfy the PSC property?
To be stand-alone, the local condition should specify that infinity may belong to S and then Q_\infty=R.
The paper’s nearby Theorem 1.3 gives evidence in low genus; your draft does not indicate that this is the exact surrounding context in the introduction.
refined_question: Let S be a finite set of places of Q, possibly including \infty, and write Q_{tot,S} for the maximal algebraic extension of Q in which every place in S totally splits, and Q_{solv} for the compositum of all finite solvable extensions of Q. Is the field K:=Q_{tot,S}\cap Q_{solv} pseudo-S-closed in the sense of Conjecture 1.1; that is, does K satisfy the corresponding S-adic local-global principle (equivalently, in the paper’s introductory formulation, does every smooth absolutely irreducible curve over K that has points over all classical closures of K above the places in S already have a K-rational point)?
justification: The draft is aimed at the solvable branch of the paper’s main introductory conjectural picture: the field under discussion is exactly an intersection of a totally S-split field with a distinguished algebraic extension of Q, and the sought property is PSC rather than mere ampleness. The introduction is the right place to anchor the reformulation because the paper flags Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 there, while §3 ("Algebraic fields") is where the arithmetic examples and open questions about such algebraic extensions are organized. The main corrections are therefore to (i) pin the question to the solvable half of Conjecture 1.1, (ii) define Q_{tot,S} and Q_{solv} exactly, and (iii) replace the broadened "every smooth Q-variety" phrasing by the paper-faithful PSC/local-global formulation used in the introduction and its nearby discussion.
